newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes unchanged against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes unchanged against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed unchanged at 8.2982 against the U.S. dollar on Thursday from the previous session's close, with trading more active due to the widening of trading limits by the central bank, traders said.

The People's Bank of China said in a statement that the limit for one transaction against the previous transaction of the Chinese yuan against the U.S. dollar and the Hong Kong dollar had been widened to 100 points against 20 points.
But the statement said daily movement limits for all the currencies traded would remain the same.

The market, establihse in 1994, has in place daily rate movement limits of 0.3 percent in either direction for the U.S. dollar against the yuan, one percent for the Hong Kong dollar and 0.3 percent for 100 Japanese yen.
Dealers said the transaction limit relaxation made trading more active today but the yuan's range-bound movement continued in this first session of 1997.
The local currency opened slightly lower at 8.2988 and consolidated around 8.2980 for most of the session, hitting a intra-day low of 8.3031 and a high of 8.2888.
Trading was active, with most done at about 8.2982, traders said.
"Today was the first session of 1997 and most traders were quite cautious, which made the yuan stay in a narrow range," one dealer said.
"The influence of the new (limits) policy has not yet been completely reflected in the yuan's movement because traders need time to get used to it," he added.
"More active trading will attract some speculative traders into the market and the prices will move in a wider range," a second dealer said.
But traders said they expect the yuan to remain very stable thanks to the unchanged limits on daily price movements and frequent central bank intervention in trading.

"Trading is expected to be more active," said one trader. "But the Chinese yuan is likely to continue to be one of the most stable currencies in the world due to the daily limits and frequent central bank intervention."
Dealers expect the yuan to consolidate just above 8.3000 on Friday.
The yuan closed up at 7.1700 in dull trading against 100 Japanese yen from 7.2000 and fell against the Hong Kong dollar to close down at an intra-day low of 1.0760 from 1.0723.
